Scaffolding explicitly reads the named standards before files exist and loads private references selectively by the listed triggers.
Ordinary services consume typed options instead of configuration keys and parsing (reported: stronger than a general preference against scattered IConfiguration use).
Abstractions are used at Application-service as well as repository/external boundaries; concrete registration is allowed for implementation helpers.
EF configuration is placed in separate IEntityTypeConfiguration classes rather than only behind an Infrastructure boundary.
When no reasonable free alternative exists say so, and draw no legal conclusions beyond the published license.

Angular guidance: investigate sanitization bypasses, match server XSRF validation, specific behavioral test targets and a small default E2E suite; NgModules must not work around standalone setup failures.

URL-segment versioning is the default; header/query versioning when requirements justify it; strategies are not mixed without a concrete reason (reported: allows mixing that 'one strategy consistently' excludes).

Versioning knowledge adds same-Application-result mapping, client-generation compatibility considerations, version-grouped documents when needed and coexistence test topics without identical duplicated tests.
Capability changes require contract mapping, full old-facet removal, fixed paths and a green structure check; provider variants require synchronized manifest, register, facets and provider tests.
Unexpected exceptions propagate to one centralized handler; the example maps client-aborted requests to HTTP 499 (reported: the example's normativity is uncertain).
Typed outcomes are named by Application/business semantics (Validation, NotFound, Conflict, BusinessRuleViolation), not HTTP names (reported: NotFound/Conflict blur the HTTP-name boundary).
Authorization tests cover denied, unauthenticated, allowed, ownership and intended anonymous behavior rather than checking attributes alone.
Repair requires reading the complete relevant output, understanding a diagnostic before changing how it is reported, stopping when progress stalls and avoiding unrelated builds.

Repairs prohibit any/strict-mode shortcuts, independently patching mismatched contracts, reflexive lockfile deletion and changing declared toolchains to suit the local machine; upgrade replacements require verified documentation.

npm floating-version detection covers only empty, *, x, latest and next; ranges and other tags pass, while listed runtime tooling always warns (reported gaps).

An approval counts only as a dated Accepted-decisions row (or a linked docs/decisions record) naming the project or the 'From -> To' edge; direction or negation of approval is not parsed (reported).
Per-file manifest-checker arguments must resolve inside the active root; warnings alone yield success and missing selected files return no findings (reported uncertainty).
npm command versions must be exact three-component semver, while local paths, URLs, git sources and archives count as pinned (reported: immutability is not examined).

Allowed references are inferred from project-name suffixes and fixed test-role tables; Api-to-Domain is allowed and unknown projects are unclassified (reported accuracy limits).
